##  — Department of Planning


### § 70. Department of Planning: Established. {#s-70}

```{=html}
<p>There is a Department of Planning, the head of which shall be the Planning Commission.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/70)


### § 71. Department of Planning: Commission – Composition; Appointment; Terms. {#s-71}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>The Planning Commission shall consist of nine members,</p>
<p>one of whom shall be the Director of Public Works ex officio,</p>
<p>one of whom shall be the Mayor of the City ex officio, and</p>
<p>one of whom shall be a member of the City Council ex officio, who shall be elected by that body, and</p>
<p>six of whom shall be appointed, must be confirmed, and shall serve, pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6</a>.</p>
<p>The terms of three appointed members shall expire on the last day of the year in which the term of the Mayor begins pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-1">Article IV, Section 1</a>, and the four year terms of three appointed members shall expire two years thereafter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">President.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor shall designate one appointed member of the Commission as its President, and may withdraw such designation and so designate another appointed member.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Designees of Mayor, Public Works Director.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor may designate a municipal officer or member of the Mayor’s personal staff to attend meetings of the Commission and to vote thereon in the Mayor’s place, and the Director of Public Works may delegate an employee in that department to attend any meeting of the Commission and to vote in the Director’s place.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Salaries.</span></p>
<p>Compensation for each of the members of the Commission, excluding those serving ex officio, except the member of the City Council, shall be set in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Qualifications.</span></p>
<p>Each member of the Commission shall be a resident and registered voter at the time, and during the term, of appointment.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/71)


### § 72. Department of Planning: Commission – Powers and duties. {#s-72}

```{=html}
<p>The Planning Commission:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span></p>
<p>shall adopt rules and regulations to exercise the powers and perform the duties of the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span></p>
<p>shall meet regularly as the Commission may determine, and hold special meetings at the call of the President or upon the written request of three members.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span></p>
<p>shall hold hearings at the Commission’s discretion or upon the written request of any member of the City Council.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span></p>
<p>may, at its hearings, administer oaths and compel the attendance of witnesses.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span></p>
<p>shall keep minutes of its proceedings and maintain a public record of its decisions, showing the vote of each member.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span></p>
<p>shall investigate and study land uses, the development of subdivisions of land, and zoning within the City of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span></p>
<p>shall adopt and revise a master plan for the proposed physical development of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span></p>
<p>before adopting or revising the master plan, shall hold a public hearing, reasonable notice of which shall be given in the neighborhood of the properties affected and by publication in a newspaper of general circulation in Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>shall consider, and may approve, if they are consistent with the master plan, among other things:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>development plans</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>an enterprise or public or private improvement that requires a permit</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">3.</span></p>
<p>urban renewal plans</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">4.</span></p>
<p>plans for the subdivision and consolidation of public and private parcels of land.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(j)</span></p>
<p>shall submit for the consideration of the Board of Estimates a recommended capital budget for inclusion in the Ordinance of Estimates, a recommended long-range capital improvement program, and a report explaining both, all of which shall be made public.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(k)</span></p>
<p>shall issue a report and recommendation, which shall state the nature of the investigation made by the Commission, whether hearings were held thereon, reasons for the recommendation, and the number of members voting for or against it:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>on every proposed amendment to the Baltimore City Zoning Ordinance referred to it; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>on the creation of, and proposed amendments to, an urban renewal plan.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(l)</span></p>
<p>may report and submit to the City Council amendments to the Baltimore City Zoning Ordinance.  Any such amendment shall be submitted only by resolution, adopted by the affirmative vote of two-thirds of the entire membership of the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(m)</span></p>
<p>shall have reasonable access, through its agents and employees, to the plats and records of all other municipal agencies of the City and, subject to the approval of the Board of Estimates, may require the assistance of any other municipal agency of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(n)</span></p>
<p>may take such other actions, subject to the provisions of this Charter and law, that it deems necessary and appropriate to assure that development is well-planned, efficiently coordinated by the City, and consistent with the health, order, security, safety and morals of the inhabitants of Baltimore City, as well as the aesthetic and natural environment of the City.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes:</strong> For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/72)


### § 73. Department of Planning: Director and staff. {#s-73}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Director – Appointment; Term.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor shall appoint a Director from a list of candidates provided by the Commission.  If, within 120 days of a vacancy in the position of Director, the Commission fails, by a majority vote of its members, to provide such a list to the Mayor, the Mayor may select the Director in the Mayor’s discretion.</p>
<p>The Director must be confirmed by the City Council pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6(a)</a>. The Mayor, after consulting with the Commission, may suspend, demote or dismiss the Director.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Staff.</span></p>
<p>The Commission shall also appoint such other employees (including part time consultants) for the conduct of the office of the Commission, as may be provided for in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Director – Qualifications.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall be qualified by personal background, education and experience to advance the development and planning of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Director – Salary.</span></p>
<p>The Director’s salary shall be set in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/73)


### § 74. Department of Planning: Master Plan. {#s-74}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Purpose.</span></p>
<p>The Master Plan shall be made for the general purpose of guiding and accomplishing a coordinated, adjusted and harmonious development of Baltimore City to promote the health, order, security, safety, and morals of its inhabitants, and to preserve and enhance the aesthetic and natural environment of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Scope.</span></p>
<p>The Master Plan may consist of a series of component plans.</p>
<p>It shall show, among other things, the future general location and extent of all public improvements and enterprises, including among other things, the general location and extent of streets, highways, boulevards, viaducts, bridges, subways, tunnels and all uses of land for purposes of public transportation, and also the general location and extent of piers, wharves, docks and bulkheads, and buildings or structures thereon, whether publicly or privately owned or operated, and also the general location and extent of publicly owned places of recreation, such as playgrounds, squares, and parks, and all public buildings and other public property, including school buildings, and all existing and proposed zoning areas or districts, and all public utilities, services and terminals, such as water, gas, electricity, sewerage, telephone, telegraph and transportation, whether privately or publicly owned or operated.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Revisions.</span></p>
<p>After the adoption of the Master Plan, or any part thereof, by the Commission, the plan may be revised only by a resolution of the Commission, carried by the affirmative vote of not less than six members of the Commission, or by ordinance adopted by the City Council by the affirmative vote of not less than three-fourths of its members.</p>
<p>An original copy of the revision, duly signed by the President, or by the Mayor if made by ordinance, shall be filed with the Department of Legislative Reference.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Conformity with Plan required.</span></p>
<p>No public improvement or enterprise, including, among other things, streets, highways, boulevards, viaducts, bridges, subways, tunnels or other uses of land for purposes of public transportation, and piers, wharves, docks, and bulkheads, and buildings or structures thereon, whether publicly or privately owned or operated, and publicly owned places of recreation, such as playgrounds, squares or parks, and public buildings, including school buildings, and public utilities, services or terminals, including gas, water, electricity, sewerage, telephone, telegraph or transportation, whether privately or publicly owned or operated, within the scope of the Master Plan shall be authorized or constructed in Baltimore City unless the location and grade thereof and, in cases of the use of land for purposes of transportation, the width thereof, shall be in conformity with the Master Plan and have been first approved by the Commission.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/74)


### § 75. Department of Planning: Subdivisions – In general. {#s-75}

```{=html}
<p>The Commission shall publish rules and regulations for the development of subdivisions which will require that development plans include adequate provision for all public improvements, enterprises and all public utilities, whether privately or publicly owned or operated; for the proper width, grade and arrangement of streets, and all uses of land for public transportation, and the relation thereof to existing streets; for adequate and convenient open spaces for traffic and the access of fire fighting apparatus; for proper drainage; and which will require that all such subdivisions and the owners thereof comply in all respects with the Master Plan.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes:</strong> For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/75)


### § 76. Department of Planning: Subdivisions – Definition. {#s-76}

```{=html}
<p>A subdivision plan shall mean a plan submitted by the owner of not less than one-third of the land included therein showing one or more new streets or parks, or showing the division of a lot, tract or parcel of land into two or more lots, tracts or parcels, or other divisions of land for the purpose, whether immediate or future, of sale or building development.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/76)


### § 77. Department of Planning: Subdivisions – Approvals. {#s-77}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Commission approval required.</span></p>
<p>All plans for subdivision of land shall be filed for record with the Commission, and no permits shall be issued by any department of the City for any work of any character whatsoever, to be done in such subdivision of land, until the plan thereof shall have been approved by the Commission as in conformity with the rules and regulations formulated and published by the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Deadline for decision.</span></p>
<p>In the event the Commission shall fail to approve or disapprove any such subdivision plan within thirty days from the date of submission thereof to the Commission, such plan shall be deemed to have been approved by the commission unless the applicant waives this requirement and consents to an extension of such period.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/77)


### § 78. Department of Planning: Subdivision regulation – Recording. {#s-78}

```{=html}
<p>Every plat showing a subdivision plan shall be filed among the Land Records of Baltimore City and with the Department of Legislative Reference, but not until after the plan has been endorsed with the approval of the Commission and of the Department of Transportation.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008; Res. 16-027, ratified Nov. 8, 2016</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/78)


### § 79. Department of Planning: Appeals. {#s-79}

```{=html}
<p>Any applicant for a permit who is aggrieved by any decision of the Commission may appeal as provided by law.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/79)


### § 80. Department of Planning: Penalties. {#s-80}

```{=html}
<p>Any person who shall violate any of the provisions or requirements of Sections 71 to 80 shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction in any court of competent jurisdiction, shall be fined as provided by law.  Every day that such violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/80)


##  — Department of Municipal and Zoning Appeals


### § 81. Department of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Established. {#s-81}

```{=html}
<p>There is a Department of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, the head of which shall be the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/81)


### § 82. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Established; Composition, etc. {#s-82}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Composition, appointment, terms, qualifications.</span></p>
<p>The Board shall consist of five members, at least one of whom shall be a lawyer, who shall be appointed, must be confirmed and shall serve pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6</a> and State law.</p>
<p>Each member of the Board shall be a registered voter and resident of the City at the time, and during the term of, appointment.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">President; Salaries.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor shall designate one member of the Board as its President and may withdraw that designation and so designate another member.</p>
<p>The salary of the President and each member of the Board shall be set in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/82)


### § 83. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: General powers and duties. {#s-83}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Meetings; Minutes; Hearings.</span></p>
<p>The Board shall hold meetings at such times as it may by rule prescribe.  Minutes shall be kept of all its proceedings, showing those present and their vote on each question submitted.  These minutes and all other records of the Board shall be public records and kept at the office of the Board.  All hearings held by the Board or its panels shall be open to the public.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Rules of proceedings.</span></p>
<p>The Board shall adopt rules for the conduct of its proceedings, which may be modified or repealed by ordinance.  The rules shall be in writing and when adopted shall be immediately filed in the office of the Board and shall be a public record.  A copy thereof (and of any amendments thereto) shall also be filed with the Department of Legislative Reference.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Zoning appeals.</span></p>
<p>The Board shall sit to hear zoning appeals.  The hearing shall be conducted by all members present and if five members of the Board are present, the concurring vote of at least four members of the Board is necessary to reverse any order, requirement, decision, or determination of an administrative official, or to decide in favor of the applicant on any matter on which it is required to pass under a zoning ordinance or to effect any variation in such ordinance.  If only four members of the Board are present, the concurring vote of at least three members is necessary to take any action under this subsection.  In other cases, the Board may sit in panels of not less than two members each and, in such cases, the concurrence of at least two members shall be required to make a decision of the Board.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Oaths and subpoenas.</span></p>
<p>The Board shall have power to administer oaths in hearings before it, to compel the attendance of witnesses and, pursuant to its rules, to require any person to answer in writing and under oath any interrogatories it may direct to such person as to any matter pending before it or subject to its action or review.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Executive Secretary; Staff.</span></p>
<p>The Board shall appoint an Executive Secretary and such other employees as may be provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Access to agency records.</span></p>
<p>The Board shall have access, through its agents and employees, to the plats and records of all other departments of the City.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes:</strong> For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/83)


### § 84. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Zoning appeals. {#s-84}

```{=html}
<p>Appeals from the Zoning Commissioner shall be determined by the Board and shall be taken pursuant to law.  Upon such appeals, the Board shall have such powers and be subject to such restrictions as may be provided by law.  The Board, after public hearing, may grant special individual exceptions to the provisions of the zoning ordinances or regulations as provided by law.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/84)


### § 85. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Paving assessments. {#s-85}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Appeal to Board.</span></p>
<p>Whenever the Department of Transportation levies an assessment or charge for the paving of a street, alley, or sidewalk under <a href="article-vii.html#s-116">§ 116 of this article</a>, the owner of the property on which the assessment or charge is levied may, within 30 days of the mailing to the owner of a notice of the assessment or charge, bring the assessment or charge to the Board for its review.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Decision.</span></p>
<p>On reasonable notice in accordance with its rules and this Charter, the Board shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>determine whether the assessment or charge is proper; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>if not, set it at the amount that the Board determines to be proper.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/85)


### § 86. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Review powers conferred by law. {#s-86}

```{=html}
<p>The Board shall have such additional powers to examine, review and revise acts or rulings of other departments and officers of the City affecting the construction, alteration, use or operation of land or buildings in the City or other charges as may from time to time be conferred upon it by law, but the powers conferred upon it in the Charter shall not be diminished or abridged by ordinance, nor may the Board be given power to review or alter determinations of the Planning Commission.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/86)


### § 87. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Additional powers conferred by law. {#s-87}

```{=html}
<p>The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals shall have and exercise all the rights, powers, duties, obligations and functions conferred by law upon the Board of Zoning Appeals not otherwise conferred by the Charter on other agencies of the City and not inconsistent with its provisions.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/87)


### § 88. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Judicial review. {#s-88}

```{=html}
<p>If any person, including the City and the Planning Commission, feeling aggrieved by any decision of the Board within thirty days of a decision by the Board, appeals therefrom to the Baltimore City Circuit Court, the Board shall forthwith transmit all papers, or copies thereof, to the court, certified by its executive secretary.</p>
<p>An appeal shall stay all proceedings in furtherance of the action appealed from.  But whenever, in the opinion of the Board, such stay would cause imminent peril to life or property, or serious public inconvenience, it may ask the Circuit Court for an order vacating such stay.  From the findings of the Circuit Court in such cases, there shall be such appeal, if any, as may be permitted by law.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/88)


### § 89. Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals: Notices; Evidence. {#s-89}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Notice of decisions.</span></p>
<p>Whenever the Board shall make a decision it shall give reasonable notice thereof by mail to all parties who, from the papers or testimony before it, seem to be parties in interest.  But failure to give such notice or of a party to receive notice of an order within thirty days of its entry shall not invalidate the decision nor, save by petition to and special order of the Board, extend the time to appeal from the order.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Evidence; Notices of proceedings.</span></p>
<p>Parties in interest who appear at a hearing before the Board shall be permitted to offer testimony pertinent to the issue or issues in which they are concerned, but the Board shall not be bound by the technical rules of evidence in force in the courts of Maryland, and may receive in evidence any paper, statement, record or other evidence, with or without prior notice to the parties, which it deems to be material and to have probative force.</p>
<p>Whatever record or notice of the proceedings or action of the Board is required by an act of the General Assembly to be given to any person or public officer shall be observed by the Board.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/89)


##  — Department of Legislative Reference


### § 90. Department of Legislative Reference:  Established. {#s-90}

```{=html}
<p>There is a Department of Legislative Reference, the head of which shall be the Director of Legislative Reference who shall supervise and direct the Department.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-011, ratified Nov. 6, 2018</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/90)


### § 91. Department of Legislative Reference:  Director – Nominating Board. {#s-91}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Ad hoc board.</span></p>
<p>There is a{n ad hoc nominating} board of the Department of Legislative Reference, which from time to time shall be established pursuant to <a href="article-vii.html#s-91">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Composition of board.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The board shall be composed of 3 members.  The Mayor, the President of the City Council, and the Comptroller shall each appoint 1 member to the board.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The board shall be appointed without regard to political affiliation, and is not subject to the requirements of <a href="article-iv.html#s-8">Article IV, § 8</a>. {“Minority party representation”} of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>No member of the board may be a City employee or an elected official other than a member of the judiciary.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>The board shall elect a chair from among its members.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Filling a vacancy.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Whenever the Mayor and the President of the City Council find that the position of Director of Legislative Reference is vacant, the board shall be appointed within 6 weeks of that finding.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The board shall be responsible for all activities by which candidates to fill the vacancy are solicited, investigated, interviewed, and recommended for appointment.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The board shall recommend no less than 2, and no more than 3, candidates for appointment to the Mayor and the President of the City Council.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>Upon the appointment of the Director of Legislative Reference, the board shall be deemed dissolved and its work completed.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-011, ratified Nov. 6, 2018</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/91)


### § 92. Department of Legislative Reference:  Director – Qualifications, Appointment, Removal, etc. {#s-92}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Qualifications.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall have substantial experience in law, legislative drafting or library administration.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Appointment.</span></p>
<p>Upon receipt of a recommendation by an ad hoc board of the Department of Legislative Reference pursuant to <a href="article-vii.html#s-91">§ 91(c) of this article</a>, a Director may be appointed by the affirmative vote of both the Mayor and the President of the City Council.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Removal.</span></p>
<p>The Director may be removed from office by the affirmative vote of both the Mayor and the President of the City Council.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Salary.</span></p>
<p>The Director’s salary shall be set in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-011, ratified Nov. 6, 2018</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/92)


### § 93. Department of Legislative Reference:  Director – Powers and Duties. {#s-93}

```{=html}
<p>The Director:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">{(i)}</span></p>
<p>
            {Legislative matters.}
          </p>
<p>shall investigate and report upon the laws of this and other states and cities relating to any subject requested by the Mayor, any committee of the City Council or the head of any department;</p>
<p>accumulate data in relation to the practical operation and effect of such laws;</p>
<p>investigate and collect all available information relating to any matter which is the subject of proposed legislation by the General Assembly of Maryland, or the City Council of Baltimore;</p>
<p>examine acts, ordinances and records of any state or city, and report the result thereof to the Mayor, any committee of the City Council or the head of any department requesting the same;</p>
<p>prepare or advise in the preparation of any bill, ordinance or resolution when requested so to do by any member of the City Council; and</p>
<p>preserve and collect all information obtained, carefully indexed and arranged so as to be at all times easily accessible to city officers and open to the inspection of the general public.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">{(ii)}</span></p>
<p>
            {Records and archives.}
          </p>
<p>shall keep all the books, documents, archives, records, official plats, papers and proceedings of the City except those in current use or whose custody the Board of Estimates shall by resolution otherwise direct or authorize;</p>
<p>carefully collect, arrange and safely keep a complete series of the ordinances, resolutions and proceedings of the City;</p>
<p>receive and keep all other documents pertaining to the City which the Director may deem of historic value or be instructed so to do by ordinance or by resolution of the Board of Estimates;</p>
<p>provide for the retention of such books, documents, papers, plats or archives in the Department, and provide for their inspection and reproduction by the public under such reasonable regulations and supervision as the Director may prescribe;</p>
<p>carefully prepare and keep an index of all books, papers, records and documents in the custody of the Department; and</p>
<p>keep a current separate index of all rules and regulations of other departments and agencies of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">{(iii)}</span></p>
<p>
            {Staff.}
          </p>
<p>may appoint such employees as may be provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">{(iv)}</span></p>
<p>
            {Duties prescribed by law.}
          </p>
<p>perform such other duties as prescribed by law.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes:</strong> 
            Resolution 18-011rewrote the preexisting §§ 90 through 93, effective January 1, 2019.  Section 3 of that Resolution, provides as follows
            [T[he Director of Legislative Reference holding office at the time the amendments to <a href="article-vii.html">Article VII</a>, Sections <a href="article-vii.html#s-90">90</a>, <a href="article-vii.html#s-91">91</a>, <a href="article-vii.html#s-92">92</a> and <a href="article-vii.html#s-93">93</a> become effective shall remain in the office until, pursuant to the amendments, reappointment or the appointment of a successor. 
          </p>
```

##  — Civil Service Commission


### § 94. Civil Service Commission: Established. {#s-94}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Appointment, term, qualifications.</span></p>
<p>There is a Civil Service Commission of three members who shall be appointed, must be confirmed and shall serve pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6</a>.</p>
<p>The terms of two members shall expire on the last day of the year in which the term of the Mayor begins pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-1">Article IV, Section 1</a>, and the four year term of the third member shall expire two years thereafter.</p>
<p>Each member of the Commission shall be a registered voter and resident of the City at the time, and during the term, of appointment.  All appointments to the Commission shall be made from persons friendly to the merit system of appointment to office.  No one holding any public office of profit shall be appointed a member of the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">President.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor shall designate one member of the Commission as its President, and may withdraw that designation and so designate another member.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Staff.</span></p>
<p>The Commission may appoint such employees as may be provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/94)


### § 95. Civil Service Commission: Powers and duties. {#s-95}

```{=html}
<p>The Commission:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span></p>
<p>shall advise the Mayor and Director on personnel matters.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span></p>
<p>shall provide to the Mayor and City Council at least annually a report on the operations of the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span></p>
<p>shall review and approve the different groupings of positions having similar duties, responsibilities and qualifications (“classifications”) that are used by the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span></p>
<p>shall promulgate and make available to the public rules governing the operation of the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span></p>
<p>shall review and approve, before they become final, and make available to the public, the rules of the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span></p>
<p>shall provide a hearing, on written request, to any non-probationary member of the Civil Service who has been discharged from the Civil Service, reduced in pay or position, or suspended for longer than 30 days.  If the Commission finds that the intent and spirit of a provision of this Charter has been violated, it shall report its findings to the Mayor; and the appointing officer shall take whatever action the Commission directs to rectify the violation.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span></p>
<p>may, if it determines after appropriate investigation, that any administrative head of the City, including any commission or board, or any officer having the power of appointment and removal in the Civil Service, has abused such power by making appointments or removals for any reason other than the good of the public service, so report to the Mayor.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span></p>
<p>may appoint such hearing officers and other employees as provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>may, in the course of hearings, administer oaths, subpoena documents, summon witnesses, and examine witnesses; and may delegate these powers to a commissioner or hearing officer.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(j)</span></p>
<p>shall render decisions within sixty days of the close of hearings unless the City employee and City both agree to an extension.  If the Commission fails to decide within the sixty day time period, the decision of the hearing officer, if there is one, shall be deemed to be the decision of the Commission.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes, History:</strong> Res. 06-017, ratified Nov. 7, 2006; For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/95)


### § 96. Civil Service Commission: Department of Human Resources – Established. {#s-96}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>There is a Department of Human Resources.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Purpose.</span></p>
<p>The Department shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>promote merit and fitness in City employment;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>ensure that appointments and promotions in the City’s Civil Service are made, and that salaries are established, without regard to political affiliation; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>promote the efficient delivery of services to the public.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 04-054, ratified Nov. 2, 2004</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/96)


### § 97. Civil Service Commission: Department of Human Resources – Powers and duties. {#s-97}

```{=html}
<p>The Department:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span></p>
<p>shall propose and submit to the Commission for final approval rules and regulations, including rules and regulations governing probationary status, temporary and emergency appointments, classifications, reclassifications, examinations, promotions, demotions, transfers, reinstatements, discharges, and other discipline of employees.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span></p>
<p>shall propose and submit to the Commission for final approval the different classifications that are used by the Department.  Such classifications shall assure that City employees are hired and promoted based on ability, efficiency, character, and industry (“merit”); and shall encourage the recruitment, training and supervision of qualified employees.  Classifications may be grouped into categories, which may include a general category for employees who are hired or promoted based, in part, on the results of competitive or non-competitive examinations; a labor category for unskilled or skilled laborers; and other categories that the Commission may deem to be appropriate.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span></p>
<p>subject to the exceptions in Section 99, shall assign to a classification each position in the City to which appointments are made.  The Department shall not assign a position outside of the Civil Service without the approval of the Civil Service Commission.  All the classified positions shall constitute the Civil Service, and appointments to positions in the Civil Service shall be made according to the rules of the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span></p>
<p>shall provide for competitive examinations, non-competitive examinations, and other evaluative measures to assure that City employees are hired based on merit.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span></p>
<p>shall provide for competitive examinations, non-competitive examinations, and other evaluative measures, including conduct in office, demonstrated capacity, and seniority, to assure that City employees are promoted based on merit.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span></p>
<p>shall promptly certify to appointing officers lists of candidates eligible for employment within each classification.  The Commission, by rule:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>shall determine when certifications shall include, in rank order, those persons who have performed best on competitive examinations and when certifications should include persons whose fitness has been otherwise established;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>shall determine when and how the appointing officer shall fill a vacancy or new position from the certifications; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">3.</span></p>
<p>may provide that honorably discharged veterans of war, including disabled veterans, may receive special credits for their service to the United States in determining the qualifications and relative standing of applicants for City positions.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span></p>
<p>shall establish a period of probation not exceeding one year during which the appointing officer may remove the employee at pleasure.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span></p>
<p>shall propose to the Board of Estimates appropriate salaries and wages for each classification.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>shall, in conjunction with the employing department, recruit, train and counsel Civil Service members.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(j)</span></p>
<p>may appoint such employees as provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(k)</span></p>
<p>shall administer employee benefits and pre-employment screening programs as directed by the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes:</strong> For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/97)


### § 98. Civil Service Commission: Department of Human Resources – Director. {#s-98}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Head of Department; Qualifications.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Director of Human Resources shall supervise and direct the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Director shall have substantial experience in personnel administration.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Appointment; Term.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall be appointed, must be confirmed, and shall serve, pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Salary.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall be paid a salary as provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 04-054, ratified Nov. 2, 2004</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/98)


### § 99. Civil Service Commission: Civil Service positions. {#s-99}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Positions included.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>All employees of the City of Baltimore, except as otherwise provided by the Charter or State law, shall be members of the Civil Service, with the exception of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">a.</span></p>
<p>elected officials and those employees whom the elected officials have designated as members of their personal staffs.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">b.</span></p>
<p>Assistant City Solicitors.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">c.</span></p>
<p>with the exception of the Director of the Department of Legislative Reference, directors, or by whatever other name the chief administrative officer may be known, and the deputy directors, of all departments of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">d.</span></p>
<p>all members of boards and commissions.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">e.</span></p>
<p>all professional employees of the Department of Education.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">f.</span></p>
<p>persons in positions of temporary or seasonal employment.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">g.</span></p>
<p>persons who, in the judgment of the Civil Service Commission, exercise policy-making discretion or occupy a position of special trust and confidence that is inconsistent with membership in the Civil Service.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>Any dispute about whether a position is within the Civil Service shall be finally resolved by the Commission.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reemployment of director or deputy.</span></p>
<p>Upon leaving a position of director or deputy director, one who relinquished Civil Service status to assume that position shall, on application and with approval of the Commission, be placed on the re-employment list for his or her former classification.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/99)


### § 100. Civil Service Commission: Discharges, etc.; Reductions in force. {#s-100}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Discharges, suspensions, reductions in pay or position.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>No person may be discharged from the Civil Service, reduced in pay or position, or suspended because of political opinions or affiliations, or for refusing to contribute to any political fund or refusing to render any political service.  But nothing in this Charter relating to the Civil Service forbids the discharge, reduction in pay or position, or suspension of an officer or employee for any just cause.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Whenever a non-probationary employee is discharged, reduced in pay or position, or suspended for more than 30 days, the appointing officer shall furnish a copy of the order of discharge, reduction, or suspension, together with a statement of the reasons for the action, to the employee and to the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The employee may contest the action by:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>requesting a hearing before the Commission; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>initiating a grievance pursuant to an applicable grievance and arbitration procedure, if any, contained in an applicable collective bargaining agreement.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>Once an employee has chosen to contest an action by electing one of the procedures specified in paragraph (3) of this subsection, the employee is bound by that election and may not subsequently choose to follow a different procedure.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>In all cases, except one in which an employee elects to contest an action through a grievance and arbitration procedure under paragraph (3)(ii) of this subsection, the Commission may, and on the written request of the employee, the Commission shall investigate the disciplinary action.  If the Commission finds that the intent and spirit of the provisions of this Charter have been violated in the discharge, reduction, or suspension, it shall report its findings to the Mayor; and the appointing officer shall take whatever action the Commission directs to rectify the violation.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reductions in force – Reemployment preference.</span></p>
<p>Each person discharged for the purpose of reducing the force and without fault shall receive a certificate so stating and all persons so discharged shall be placed on the eligible list in the order of the length of their service in their classifications at the time of being laid off and in other classifications the civil service in which they may have served previously.  The weight to be given to length of service in their last classification and in prior classifications shall be determined in accordance with the rules of the Commission.  Persons so discharged shall have preference in the order of their seniority over others on the eligible list, subject, however, to the terms of the next subsection and to any priority to which any person may be entitled by virtue of any preference to veterans or their dependents.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reductions in force – Seasonal and part-time employees.</span></p>
<p>In the case of classes of seasonal or part-time employees the Commission, after notice and a public hearing, may adopt rules excluding them from, or limiting the application to them of, the preference contained in the preceding subsection.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes, History:</strong> Res. 06-017, ratified Nov. 7, 2006; 
            Section 2 of Resolution 06-017 states
            [T]his amendment applies only to grievance and arbitration procedures that, after the effective date of this amendment, have been adopted as part of a collective bargaining agreement to apply to employees who have been discharged, reduced in pay or position, or suspended for more than 30 days.
          ; For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/100)


### § 101. Civil Service Commission: Roster of Service employees. {#s-101}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Commission to keep; Contents.</span></p>
<p>The Commission shall keep in its office an official roster of the Civil Service, and shall enter thereon the name of every person who has been appointed, employed, promoted, reduced, transferred or reinstated in any Civil Service position.</p>
<p>This roster shall be open to public inspection at all reasonable hours, and shall show in connection with each name the date of appointment, employment, promotion, reduction, transfer or reinstatement and the compensation of the position, its title, the nature of the duties thereof and the date and cause of any termination of such office or employment.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reports to Commission.</span></p>
<p>It shall be the duty of each appointing officer to report to the Commission forthwith, upon the appointment or employment of any person in the Civil Service, the name of the appointee or employee, the title and character of the office or employment, the date of commencement of service, and to report the separation of a person from the service, or other change in status and other information that the Civil Service Commission may require in order to keep the roster.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Salary contingent on roster listing.</span></p>
<p>It shall be unlawful, after notice from the Commission for the Department of Finance to pay any salary or compensation to any officer, clerk, employee or other person in the Civil Service whose name does not appear upon the roster as being in the employ of the City.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/101)


### § 102. Civil Service Commission: Political contributions. {#s-102}

```{=html}
<p>No person in the Civil Service shall for any reason be under any obligation to contribute to any political fund, and no person shall knowingly, directly or indirectly, in person or by letter, request or solicit the payment of any political assessment, subscription or contribution from any person in the Civil Service.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/102)


### § 103. Civil Service Commission: Abolished positions. {#s-103}

```{=html}
<p>Any person holding any position in the Civil Service which may be abolished by the adoption of any amendment to the Charter or in any other lawful manner, shall be placed upon the reemployment list for the classification to which the abolished position belonged in accordance with Sections 100 and 101; or if no position of the same classification as that of the position abolished shall remain in the Civil Service after the abolition of the position, the person shall be placed on the reemployment list for a position that, in the judgment of the Civil Service Commission, shall most nearly approximate the position abolished.</p>
<p>No position shall be deemed to be abolished by reason of being transferred or placed in or under a different municipal agency without substantial change in the nature of the actual duties of the position.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/103)


### § 104. Civil Service Commission: Penalties. {#s-104}

```{=html}
<p>Any violation of any of the provisions of the Charter relating to the Civil Service, or any willful use of any corrupt means in connection with any examination, appointment, promotion, reduction, transfer or reinstatement shall be deemed a misdemeanor and, upon conviction in a court of competent jurisdiction, shall be punished by a fine or by imprisonment as provided by law.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/104)


##  — Board of Ethics


### § 105. Board of Ethics: State Code requirements. {#s-105}

```{=html}
<p>The Mayor and City Council of Baltimore shall adopt ordinances to execute the provisions of “the Maryland Public Ethics Law” of the Annotated Code of Maryland to be administered by the Board of Ethics.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/105)


### § 106. Board of Ethics: Established; Composition. {#s-106}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Board established.</span></p>
<p>There is a Board of Ethics to be known as the Board of Ethics of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Composition.</span></p>
<p>The Board of Ethics shall consist of five members:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Three members shall be appointed by the Mayor in conformity with <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Section 6 of Article IV</a> of the Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>The Mayor and the City Solicitor are members ex officio with full voting powers.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>The Mayor may designate a municipal official appointed by him under the provisions of <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Section 6 of Article IV</a> of the Charter to serve in his position as a member with full voting powers.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>The City Solicitor may designate a member of the Solicitor’s staff to serve in his position as a member with full voting powers.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Term of ex officio members.</span></p>
<p>The City Solicitor and the Mayor or their designees on the Board shall only serve during the time that the Mayor or City Solicitor holds elected or appointed office.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/106)


### § 107. Board of Ethics: Member qualifications. {#s-107}

```{=html}
<p>A person is eligible to serve as a member of the Board if:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the person is of known personal integrity;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>the person possesses a recognized knowledge and interest in government and civics;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>the person is not required to file as a lobbyist under <a href="article-vii.html">this article</a>;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>except as provided in this subtitle of the Charter, the person is not an elected official, municipal officer, or municipal employee.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/107)


### § 108. Board of Ethics: Term, vacancies, chair, meetings, etc. {#s-108}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Terms.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The term of members appointed under the provision of Section 106 of this subtitle of the Charter is five years or until their successors are appointed and qualify.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The terms of initial appointees shall be arranged so that no more than one shall expire in any year.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Vacancies.</span></p>
<p>Any vacancy occurring on the Board shall be filled for the unexpired term in the same manner as the original appointment to the vacant office.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Removal.</span></p>
<p>Members of the Board may be removed pursuant to the provisions of <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6</a> of the Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Chair.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor shall designate a member of the Board as chairman.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Quorum.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>A quorum consists of three members.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>An affirmative vote of at least three members shall be necessary for any action of the Board.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Compensation.</span></p>
<p>The members of the Board shall serve without compensation.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Open meetings.</span></p>
<p>Except as provided in <a href="article-vii.html">this article</a>, meetings of the Board shall be conducted under the Meetings of Public Bodies provisions of the Annotated Code of Maryland.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Records.</span></p>
<p>The records of the Board shall show the vote of each member on each question.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Disqualification on candidacy.</span></p>
<p>A person shall not be a member of the Board if the member becomes a candidate for elected public office of the United States, the State, the City, or any county or municipality of the State.</p>
</div>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/108)


### § 109. Board of Ethics: Powers and duties. {#s-109}

```{=html}
<p>Powers, duties, administration, and other provisions relating to the Board of Ethics shall be set out in the ordinances constituting the Baltimore City Ethics Law.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/109)


### § 110. Chair: Powers and duties. {#s-110}

```{=html}
<p>The Chair of the Board of Ethics shall have exclusive authority to select at random the 11 members of the advisory board to appoint the Inspector General, as described in <a href="article-x.html#s-2">Article X, Section 2</a> of this Charter.</p>
<p>In the event a vacancy occurs on the advisory board, the Chair shall be authorized to fill the vacancy through the process outlined in <a href="article-x.html#s-2">Article X, Section 2</a> of this Charter.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/110)


### § 111. Board of Ethics: Modification by ordinance. {#s-111}

```{=html}
<p>The Mayor and City Council, by ordinance, may modify, amend, alter, clarify or implement any or all of the provisions of Sections <a href="article-vii.html#s-105">105</a> through <a href="article-vii.html#s-111">111</a> of <a href="article-vii.html">this </a><a href="article-vii.html">Article VII</a>.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/111)
