##  — Department of Transportation


### § 114. Department established. {#s-114}

```{=html}
<p>There is a Department of Transportation, the head of which is the Director of Transportation.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 04-056, ratified Nov. 2, 2004</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/114)


### § 115. Director of Transportation. {#s-115}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Duties; Qualifications.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Director shall supervise and direct the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Director must have substantial administrative experience in transportation or in the delivery of related public service.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Appointment; Term.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall be appointed, must be confirmed, and serves pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, § 6</a> of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Salary.</span></p>
<p>The Director’s salary shall be set in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Employees.</span></p>
<p>The Director may appoint the  employees provided for in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 04-056, ratified Nov. 2, 2004</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/115)


### § 116. Powers and duties of Department. {#s-116}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Charter, the Department has the following powers and duties.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Street construction and maintenance.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Department has charge of constructing and maintaining the streets of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Department shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>prepare the plans and perform the work required by Ordinances for opening, extending, widening, straightening, grading, and closing any street in the City; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>prepare all Ordinances for the opening and closing of streets, attend the hearings on  those Ordinances, and perform all administrative functions related to those Ordinances.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>Before paving or repaving a street, the Director of Transportation shall give notice in one or more daily City newspapers that, not less than 90 days from the first publication date, the Department will proceed with the paving or repaving and warning all persons to obtain permits for and to complete before that day all work that might involve the digging up of the street.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>The Director shall send a copy of this notice to all persons who the Director has reason to believe would be interested in receiving it, but failure to send the notice does not affect the validity of any action taken by the Mayor and the Director t pave or repave a street.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>No pavement laid after the publication of the notice may be dug up by any person without a permit issued by the Director.  The Director has discretion to issue or withhold this permit, and may attach appropriate conditions and charges to the permit.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>Whenever an assessment or charge is to be made against a property for paving a street, alley, or sidewalk, the Department after giving the owner of the property involved due notice and an opportunity to be heard, shall fix the amount of the assessment or charge.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Lighting.</span></p>
<p>The Department has charge of the lighting of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Conduit system.</span></p>
<p>The Department may exercise all the powers and shall perform all the duties relating to the conduit system, and has charge of all property and equipment pertaining to that system.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Approval of new streets.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Any person who, in connection with any real estate development, wants to lay out, locate, or construct a street, public or private, within Baltimore City shall, before beginning construction and before selling any land abutting on the street, present to the Department a copy of the plat for the proposed development, as approved by the Planning Commission, showing in detail the proposed streets.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>If the plat is approved by the Department, the person shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>record a copy of the plat, with the endorsements of the Planning Commission and the Department on it, with the Clerk of the Circuit Court of Baltimore City; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>a certified copy of the recorded plat with the Department.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Street names.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>New public streets may not be designated by names until the names have been approved by the Department and entered on the appropriate plats and records of the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>If a private street is dedicated for public purposes and the dedication is accepted, or if the title to a private street is conveyed to the City, the Department shall give the street a name, by which it shall be known on all official records of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The name of a public street may not be changed except by ordinance or resolution of the Mayor and City Council</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Building numbers.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Department:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>shall determine and fix the number of every new building; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>may change existing numbers.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Department shall report each new number or change of number to the owner or occupant of the building.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Street plats and plans.</span></p>
<p>The Department shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>adopt rules and regulations regarding plats and plans relating to the location of streets; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>shall prepare these plats and plans as required by the Board of Estimates or by ordinance.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Plats and records – Underground structures.</span></p>
<p>The Department shall maintain plats and records of tunnels, pipes, mains, sewers, conduits, and other underground structures, both public and private.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(j)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Plats and records – Properties.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Department shall maintain adequate plats and other records of all parcels of real property within Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>These plats and records shall include:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the ownership of each parcel; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the symbol by which each parcel is identified.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>These plats and records shall be the official plats and records to be used by all municipal agencies to identify and determine the location of every parcel of real property within Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(k)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">System of uniform property identification.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Department shall maintain a system for the uniform identification of all real property within Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The system shall identify each parcel of real property by a symbol.  That symbol shall be used by every municipal agency to identify that parcel, until it is subdivided or the symbol is changed by the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The failure of the Department or of any other municipal agency to identify a parcel of property by its symbol does not affect the validity of any assessment or charge otherwise properly made.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(l)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Additional powers and duties.</span></p>
<p>The Department has the additional powers and duties relating to the construction, reconstruction, and maintenance of streets, to transportation, and to traffic, including powers and duties transferred from other municipal agencies, as are prescribed by law.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes, History:</strong> Res. 04-056, ratified Nov. 2, 2004; Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008; Res. 14-016, ratified Nov. 4, 2014; For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/116)


### § 116A. Assessment of benefits and damages. {#s-116a}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Elements of enabling ordinance.</span></p>
<p>An ordinance to open, extend, widen, straighten, close, or grade any street, alley, or footway in Baltimore City may provide that the benefits assessed may be paid in not more than 5 annual installments, with interest at a rate determined just and proper by the Director of Transportation, with the concurrence of the Board of Estimates, on all deferred installments, accounting from the date that, under <a href="article-vii.html#s-116a">subsection (e) of this section</a>, the first annual installment would become in arrears if unpaid.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Notice to Finance, owner.</span></p>
<p>When the physical work required by the ordinance is completed:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the Department of Transportation shall notify the Director of Finance that the work has been completed; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>the Department of Finance shall give written notice to the property owner:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>that the work has been completed;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>that the benefits assessed for the work are due; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>how the owner may obtain a hearing on the assessment.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Payment for benefits.</span></p>
<p>If the ordinance does not provide otherwise, all benefits assessed shall be payable, at the option of the property owner, either at once or in 5 equal annual installments.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Damages.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>If, in any proceedings, the same person is assessed for benefits and also awarded damages, the damages shall be deducted from the benefits, and the provisions of <a href="article-vii.html#s-116a">this section</a> as to payment of benefits apply only to the excess of the benefits over the damages.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The damages awarded to any person in connection with the project shall be payable at the time or times provided in the ordinance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>No part of any street, alley, or footway may be physically opened, extended, widened, or straightened on or over the ground of any person determined by the Department of Transportation to be entitled to damages for the alteration without the written consent of that person, unless the damages have been paid to that person or paid into a special account to the credit of that person.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Lien for benefits; Arrearage.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>An assessment by the Department of Transportation on benefitted property is a lien on that property, in the full amount of the assessment, from the date the Department of Transportation notifies the Director of Finance that the physical work required has been completed until the assessment is paid to the Director of Finance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Benefits assessed or, if payable in installments, the first installment, are due and payable on the date when the Director of Finance notifies the property owner of the assessment, and are in arrears 6 months from that date.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Sale on default.</span></p>
<p>If the assessment on a property is in arrears, the Director of Finance shall proceed to sell that property in accordance with and subject to the same conditions imposed by the laws governing the sale of real estate charged with the payment of City taxes.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Resale on purchaser’s default.</span></p>
<p>If the tax-sale purchaser fails to comply with the terms of the sale, the Director of Finance shall resell the property at the risk of the former purchaser.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Refunds of assessment.</span></p>
<p>If an ordinance providing for the opening, extending, widening, grading, or closing of a street, alley, or footway is invalidated by a court of competent jurisdiction or is repealed, the Director of Finance shall promptly:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>refund all assessments paid under the invalidated ordinance; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>pay all expenses incurred, including reasonable attorney’s fees, and for which the City is liable in carrying out the ordinance.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/116A)


### § 116B. Correcting physical obstruction. {#s-116b}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Correction required.</span></p>
<p>Any person who has, in, over, or under a public street in Baltimore City, any building, structure, conduit, drain, main, pipe, track, work, or other physical obstruction that blocks or impedes the work of the Department shall, on reasonable notice from the Department, promptly shift, adjust, or remove it, at that person’s expense, to fully meet the exigencies described in the notice.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Condemnation.</span></p>
<p>The City is empowered, when the exigencies of the Department’s work require, to secure the condemnation of the physical obstruction as provided in <a href="article-ii.html">Article II</a> of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/116B)


##  — Compensation Commission for Elected Officials


### § 117. Definitions. {#s-117}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>In this subtitle, the following terms have the meanings indicated.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Commission.</span></p>
<p>“Commission” means the Compensation Commission for Elected Officials.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Compensation.</span></p>
<p>“Compensation” means all salary and allowances paid to an elected official.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Elected official.</span></p>
<p>“Elected official” means:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the Mayor;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>the City Comptroller;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>the President of the City Council; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>the Members of the City Council.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/117)


### § 118. Commission established. {#s-118}

```{=html}
<p>There is a Compensation Commission for Elected Officials.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/118)


### § 119. Composition; Qualifications; Term. {#s-119}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Composition.</span></p>
<p>The Commission comprises the following 7 members:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>3 members appointed by the Mayor in accordance with <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, § 6</a> of this Charter;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>1 member appointed by the City Comptroller, subject to confirmation by the  City Council in the same manner as provided in <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, § 6</a> of this Charter for appointments by the Mayor; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>3 members appointed by the President of the City Council, subject to confirmation by the  City Council in the same manner as provided in <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, § 6</a> of this Charter for appointments by the Mayor.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">City officials, employees ineligible.</span></p>
<p>No official or employee of the City may be appointed to or serve on the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Term.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>A member of the Commission serves for a term of 4 years, beginning October 1 of the second year preceding the mayoral general election, and until a successor is appointed and qualifies.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Members of the Commission are eligible for reappointment.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/119)


### § 120. Compensation; Expenses. {#s-120}

```{=html}
<p>Members of the Commission:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>serve without compensation; but</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>are entitled to reimbursement of reasonable expenses incurred, as provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/120)


### § 121. Officers. {#s-121}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Chair.</span></p>
<p>The Commission shall elect a chair from among its members.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Others.</span></p>
<p>The Commission may elect a Vice-Chair and other officers from among its members.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/121)


### § 122. Meetings. {#s-122}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Quorum.</span></p>
<p>5 members of the Commission constitute a quorum.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Votes for action.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>An affirmative vote of at least 4 members is needed for any action by the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Commission’s records must show how each member voted on each question.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Open Meetings.</span></p>
<p>All meetings of the Commission must be conducted in accordance with the Open Meetings Act, State Government Article Title 10, Subtitle 5 {now Title 3 of the State General Provisions Article}.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/122)


### § 123. Commission recommendations. {#s-123}

```{=html}
<p>The Commission shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>evaluate the compensation of all elected officials; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>recommend that, for the next term of office, the compensation be increased, decreased, or remain unchanged.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/123)


### § 124. Submission to Council. {#s-124}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">When required.</span></p>
<p>The Commission shall submit to the President of the City Council its recommendations on or before October 1 of the year preceding the mayoral general election.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">If change proposed.</span></p>
<p>If the Commission recommends one or more changes in compensation, the President of the City Council shall cause all of the recommendations to be introduced at the next meeting of the City Council as a proposed Resolution of the Mayor and City Council.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">If no change proposed.</span></p>
<p>If the Commission recommends no change in any elected official’s compensation, or fails to submit a timely recommendation, no Resolution is to be introduced and the compensation to be paid elected officials remains unchanged.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/124)


### § 125. Council action. {#s-125}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Amendment not authorized.</span></p>
<p>The Council may not amend the Resolution to change or affect any recommended compensation.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Rejection by Council.</span></p>
<p>If, by a majority vote of all members, the City Council affirmatively rejects the Resolution on or before December 15 of the year preceding the mayoral general election, the compensation to be paid elected officials remains unchanged.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Adoption by Council.</span></p>
<p>If the Resolution is adopted on or before December 15 of the year preceding the mayoral general election, or if the City Council fails to adopt or reject the Resolution on or before that date, the compensation recommended by the Commission will apply, effective at the beginning of the next term of office.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/125)


##  — Department of General Services


### § 130. Department established. {#s-130}

```{=html}
<p>There is a Department of General Services, the head of which is the Director of General Services.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/130)


### § 131. Director of General Services. {#s-131}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Duties; Qualifications.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Director shall supervise and direct the Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Director must have:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>substantial experience in the construction and maintenance of public works and improvements and in the delivery of related public services; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>10 years experience as an engineer.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Appointment; Term.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall be appointed, must be confirmed, and serves pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, § 6</a> of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Salary.</span></p>
<p>The Director’s salary shall be set in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Employees.</span></p>
<p>The Director may appoint the employees provided for in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/131)


### § 132. Powers and duties of Department. {#s-132}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>The Department has the powers and duties specified in <a href="article-vii.html#s-132">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Supervision of municipal buildings, related improvements.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Unless otherwise provided by this Charter, the Director shall supervise all municipal buildings and related improvements made in Baltimore City or elsewhere by or for the City or any municipal agency.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>All plans and specifications for these municipal buildings and related improvements, including those involving engineering questions, shall be submitted to the Director for approval.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Construction, maintenance, etc., of buildings, related improvements.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Unless otherwise provided by this Charter, the Department has charge of the construction, demolition, alteration, operation and maintenance of all municipal buildings and related improvements.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>To carry out these activities, the Director may enter and occupy any municipal property after giving due notice to the agency having control of the property.  The Director shall restore any property so entered to the condition in which it was before the entry.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d) – (f)</span></p>
<p>Repealed by Res. 14-016, ratified Nov. 4, 2014.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Fleet management.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Department is responsible for:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the maintenance, repair, and operation of all motor vehicles and related equipment owned by the City, whether held for general service or assigned for the use of a particular office or agency,</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the maintenance and operation of related garages, depots, and shops;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>the inspection of all City vehicles and related equipment and the keeping of proper records about how these vehicles and equipment are handled and operated;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>the assignment of these vehicles and related equipment for the use of officers and other agencies of the City; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(v)</span></p>
<p>the maintenance or the hiring of any hauling or passenger service needed by any municipal agency.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>This subsection does not apply to motor vehicles and related equipment of the Baltimore City Public School System, except to the extent requested by that department and agreed to by the Department of General Services.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Assistance to other agencies.</span></p>
<p>On the request of the head of a municipal agency, the Director shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>supply estimates of the cost of work for building improvements and vehicles to be done for that agency during the next fiscal year; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>perform services for the municipal agency of the same general character as those carried on by the Department, the cost of which shall be charged to the agency requesting the services and shall be paid out of the funds appropriated to it.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Additional powers and duties.</span></p>
<p>The Department has the additional powers and duties as are prescribed by law.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/132)

```{=html}
<p>Repealed by Res. 14-016, ratified Nov. 4, 2014.</p>
```

### § 134. Correcting physical obstruction. {#s-134}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Correction required.</span></p>
<p>Any person who has, in, over, or under a public street in Baltimore City, any building, structure, conduit, drain, main, pipe, track, work, or other physical obstruction that blocks or impedes the work of the Department shall, on reasonable notice from the Department, promptly shift, adjust, or remove it, at that person’s expense, to fully meet the exigencies described in the notice.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Condemnation.</span></p>
<p>The City is empowered, when the exigencies of the Department’s work require, to secure the condemnation of the physical obstruction as provided in <a href="article-ii.html">Article II</a> of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 08-003, ratified Nov. 4, 2008</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/134)


##  — City Administrator


### § 135. City Administrator: Establishment. {#s-135}

```{=html}
<p>There is a City Administrator who shall be the chief administrative officer of the City.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 20-026, ratified Nov. 3, 2020, eff. July 1, 2021</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/135)


### § 136. City Administrator: Appointment, term, etc. {#s-136}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Appointment.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor shall appoint the City Administrator without regard to political affiliation, subject to confirmation by the City Council, pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6(a)</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Qualifications.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The City Administrator must have, prior to appointment, at least 5 years of administrative experience that is sufficiently broad, responsible, and technical to function as the City Administrator.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The City Administrator shall also be thoroughly familiar with modern accounting methods and budget procedures.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>In determining and assessing the qualifications for appointment as the City Administrator, the Mayor must give full consideration to:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the depth, breadth, quality, and importance of relevant experience and the degree of progression achieved;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the individual’s education background;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>evidence of the individual’s  demonstrated ability to accept and successfully meet increasing responsibilities; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>evidence of the individual’s excellent character, professional reputation, and employment record.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>To assure the selection of the most qualified individual available, the Mayor may retain any recognized testing agency to evaluate and make recommendations concerning the qualifications of prospective appointees.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Term.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Subject to paragraph (2) of this subsection, the City Administrator’s term shall be coterminous to the Mayor.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The City Administrator may continue to serve beyond the Mayor’s term until a qualified successor is appointed and confirmed.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Salary.</span></p>
<p>The City Administrator’s salary shall be set in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 20-026, ratified Nov. 3, 2020, eff. July 1, 2021</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/136)


### § 137.  {#s-137}

```{=html}
<p>Reserved</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/137)


### § 138. City Administrator: Removal. {#s-138}

```{=html}
<p>The Mayor may remove the City Administrator at any time.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 20-026, ratified Nov. 3, 2020, eff. July 1, 2021</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/138)


### § 139. City Administrator: Office administration. {#s-139}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Staff.</span></p>
<p>The City Administrator may appoint employees to assist in his or her duties as may be provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Deputy City Administrator.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The City Administrator shall appoint a Deputy City Administrator who shall serve as the Acting City Administrator in the event that the City Administrator is temporarily unavailable for duty or if the position has been vacated.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>A Deputy City Administrator may not serve as an Acting City Administrator longer than 6 months without confirmation by the City Council, pursuant to <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6(a)</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 20-026, ratified Nov. 3, 2020, eff. July 1, 2021</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/139)


### § 140. City Administrator: Powers and duties. {#s-140}

```{=html}
<p>Except as otherwise provided in this Charter and under the direct authority and supervision of the Mayor, the City Administrator:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>administers the day-to-day operations of the City and oversees the delivery of municipal services;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>exercises supervisory authority over all agencies, department directors, and municipal officers;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>approves rules and regulations proposed by municipal departments and agencies;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>supervises the preparation of the City’s preliminary operating budget and participates in the development of the proposed Ordinance of Estimates;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>advises the Mayor in the formation of policy and the implementation of plans to address demands for municipal services, enhance the quality of life, and strengthen the economic vitality of the City;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>performs duties delegated by the Mayor that are not inconsistent with this Charter; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>performs any other duty as required by this Charter or required by ordinance of the Mayor and City Council.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 20-026, ratified Nov. 3, 2020, eff. July 1, 2021</p>
```

[View this section on the City site](https://codes.baltimorecity.gov/us/md/cities/baltimore/charter/VII/140)

### § 141. Department established. {#s-141}

```{=html}
<p>There is a Baltimore City Police Department, the head of which is the Police Commissioner.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-003, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```
